A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TPA/T6 research. Their main text, equations, tables, rendered figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original FineWeb-Edu pretraining results and zero-shot and two-shot benchmark evaluations for small, medium and large models.

after.justification: v3 retains original training and benchmark results and adds XL-model experiments, non-contextual-factor comparisons and rank ablations.

M1.justification: The standard TPA equations and T6 block are retained, but v3 adds an alternative attention procedure that avoids materializing Q, K and V (Appendix A), and a higher-order TPA variant with an additional contextual factor (Appendix B). These are proposed extensions; the PDFs do not establish their use in the reported standard T6 experiments.

E1.justification: Both use FineWeb-Edu and the same nine downstream benchmarks: ARC-E, ARC-C, BoolQ, HellaSwag, OBQA, PIQA, WinoGrande, MMLU and SciQ. Larger models and rank sweeps add configurations, not new datasets, tasks or context-length test scenarios.

E2.justification: MHA, MQA, GQA and MLA remain evaluated comparators. The previously described non-contextual-A TPA variant becomes an evaluated comparator in small and medium experiments (v3 Tables 2, 6, 8 and 9). MFA is added only to related work, not to the experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: v3 substantially expands evaluated configurations with 1.55B-parameter, 48-layer XL models and XL KV-rank settings of 2, 4 and 6. Existing datasets, metrics and zero-/two-shot procedures remain. The medium-model learning rates of 3e-4 and 6e-4 were both already evaluated in v1; their main-experiment and ablation roles are exchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds direct tests of contextual versus non-contextual head factors and an XL KV-rank sensitivity study with curves and benchmark results (Appendix G.2.2, Figure 5, Tables 7 and 11). These examine central factorization choices that v1's learning-rate ablation did not address. The learning-rate analysis is retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point benchmark scores and training/validation curves without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The additional results retain this reporting practice.

E6.justification: v3 adds XL, rank-sweep and non-contextual-A results and revises existing MLA scores. For large-model two-shot evaluation, MLA's reported average changes from 54.36 to 55.74, now exceeding TPA-KV-only's unchanged 55.33 (v1 Table 5; v3 Table 10). At the matched medium 6e-4 setting, GQA ARC-E changes from 28.67 to 58.67 (v1 Table 10; v3 Table 2).

T1.justification: v3 adds extensive computation-cost derivations, including the condition RqRk(dh+h) <= hdh for reducing QK computation. It also defines higher-order factorization and introduces Theorem 2 and its proof under a specified Kronecker-structured rotation. The original RoPE theorem and proof are retained and relocated.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same central claims: contextual TPA factorization, the T6 architecture, unification of existing attention mechanisms, RoPE compatibility, reduced KV caching and improved model quality.

C2.justification: Section 3.5 introduces computational-efficiency claims, including at least 10x faster QK calculation than MLA based on operation counts. Appendix A adds rank, kernel and hardware qualifications for realized speedups. Appendix B discusses higher-order capacity/memory trade-offs, and Appendix G interprets increased KV rank as beneficial.

D1.justification: v3 documents the added XL configuration, including eight A100 GPUs, microbatch size 6, accumulation count 10, 48 layers, width 1600 and mechanism-specific head counts (Tables 4–5). Existing initialization, optimizer and code-access information is retained, with earlier experimental details moved from Appendix B to G.

R1.justification: v3 adds Hu et al.'s Multi-matrix Factorization Attention and explains its relationship to MQA and TPA, including Appendix E.4. It removes the cross-layer-sharing and Eigen Attention discussion and associated references. The low-rank-adaptation discussion is relocated to Appendix D rather than removed.

P1.justification: The document is substantially reorganized: MQA/GQA/MLA background moves to Appendix E, other TPA variants to F, and low-rank related work to D. Section 3.5 becomes Computational Cost, and the appendix hierarchy is rebuilt. Much of the abstract, core method prose and conclusion remains closely matched.

P2.justification: The training and validation figures are regrouped from model-specific pairs into separate three-panel displays across medium, large and XL scales. Perplexity plots move to the appendix and gain an XL panel; a new rank-ablation figure is added. Two-shot tables move to the appendix, and tables gain XL configurations and non-contextual-A rows.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens empirical support through XL experiments, contextual-factor controls and rank ablations, and aligns the medium-model main tables with their discussion. However, the added theory introduces inconsistencies: Appendix A.7 claims value-side FLOP savings under Rv << h despite its accumulation cost retaining an Rv multiplier, and Theorem 2 equates R_t ⊗ I_dc with a generally different block-diagonal matrix of repeated R_t blocks. These useful empirical gains and new problems in the theoretical justification leave the overall net quality change uncertain.
